chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Jamīl ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man entered ihram from the appointed place and proceeded on his way. Then, a day or two later, he purchased a sacrificial camel, marked it, garlanded it, and drove it along. So he said: “If he bought it before entering the Haram, there is no harm.”

I said: Then if he bought it before reaching the miqat from which he enters ihram, then marked it and garlanded it, does that make obligatory upon him what is obligatory upon the muhrim at that point? He said: “No. But when he reaches the miqat, then let him enter ihram, then mark it and garland it, for his first garlanding is of no consequence.”

key_terms.أَحْرَمَ: entered into the state of ihram
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: the person in the state of ihram
key_terms.الْوَقْتِ: the appointed place or point for entering ihram in this context
key_terms.بَدَنَةً: a sacrificial camel offered in hajj
key_terms.تَقْلِيدَهُ: his act of garlanding the sacrificial animal
key_terms.فَأَشْعَرَهَا: he marked the sacrificial animal by making the known sign on it
key_terms.وَقَلَّدَهَا: he garlanded the sacrificial animal as a ritual designation

ai.seo_question: Does marking and garlanding a sacrificial camel before the miqat make a person subject to the rules of ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith explains a legal ruling related to hajj offerings and the timing of entering ihram. It clarifies that marking and garlanding the sacrificial animal before reaching the miqat does not establish the rulings of ihram, and that the valid procedure begins after reaching the miqat and entering ihram.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.2573 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Jamil ibn Salih, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (as): "A man enters Ihram from the Miqat and proceeds on his journey. Then, a day or two later, he purchases a sacrificial camel, marks it, garlands it, and drives it forward. What is the ruling?"
Imam (as) said: "If he purchased it before entering the Haram, there is no harm."
I asked: "What if he purchased it before reaching the Miqat where he enters Ihram, marked it, and garlanded it? Does what is obligatory upon a Muhrim apply to him at that point?"
Imam (as) said: "No. However, when he reaches the Miqat, he should enter Ihram and then mark and garland it. The earlier garlanding does not hold any significance."
